clue.text: Philosopher working for detachment

parts.note: Plato, the ancient Greek philosopher
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A thinker values working in detachment from the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detachment' looks like aloofness, but here it is the military sense: a small body of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a military unit, a detachment of soldiers under a lieutenant.

clue.text: Born lumberjack who puts up posts?

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for born, as in genealogies
a logger fells trees for timber

explanation.surface: A natural woodsman is the one who puts up fence posts.
explanation.walkthrough: The posts are not fence posts from the lumberjack's timber but entries on a website.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes a weblog regularly puts up online posts, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Supporter backed it, helping the resolution of disputes

indicators.note: backed means the supporter's word is turned round, read from its end

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
taken as written
a helping or portion of food is a ration

explanation.surface: A backer returned it, assisting in settling quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbitration is the settling of a disagreement by an impartial third party.

clue.text: Stable boy left wanting promotion

parts.note: an advertisement, or ad, promotes a product

explanation.surface: A young stable hand has gone without being promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting promotion' reads as lacking advancement; 'wanting' is only a link and the promotion is an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad is the racing term for a stable hand who looks after horses.

clue.text: Skill seen in odd pieces from screen writer

indicators.note: seen in places the word for skill inside the letters picked out
odd pieces from asks for the first, third and fifth letters of the next word

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Craft shows in fragments of a screenwriter's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd pieces from' takes S, R, E from 'screen'; ART goes inside. 'Screen writer' tempts as a single idea, but 'writer' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Sartre was a French novelist, playwright and philosopher, so a writer.

clue.text: Broadcast in sound to appear as something transmitted down line

indicators.note: in sound tells us that a word spoken out loud gives letters spelt differently

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
to loom is to appear, often menacingly

explanation.surface: A transmission is heard as a signal sent down a telephone line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' is not a cable but a family line of descent.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a family possession handed down through the generations of a line.

clue.text: Aim cryptically for something quite special

parts.note: the word Aim is read as letters: I, which is one, sits within A and M, which stand for a and million

explanation.surface: Aim cleverly for something exceptional.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the Roman numeral-style abbreviation for million and I is one, so Aim shows one inside 'a M'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare and exceptional is said to be one of a kind, a rarity among very many.

clue.text: I ran Spectator puzzles stall

indicators.note: puzzles here is a verb meaning confuses, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: I ran the Spectator magazine's puzzles section to delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzles' sounds like the magazine's crossword page, but it is the anagram signal; the definition 'stall' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to put off action, to delay deliberately.

clue.text: Hunts, etc, ruined horse

indicators.note: ruined means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Fox hunts and the like have spoiled a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a horse of a reddish-brown colour.

clue.text: Bank chases Middle East business

indicators.note: chases means follows behind, so the bank word comes after

parts.note: a bank is a row or tier, as of seats or oars

explanation.surface: A bank is pursuing commercial interests in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests finance, but it is a row, a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A métier is one's trade or line of work, a business.

clue.text: Row at heart of company's ruling committee

indicators.note: at heart of means only the centre of the word survives, the ends being shed

parts.note: a company's board of directors governs it

explanation.surface: An argument at the centre of the company's board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; it is the verb to propel a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To row a boat is to pull an oar, and oar is used as a verb for rowing.

clue.text: Fool I took in during university days not formally introduced?

indicators.note: during places the fool, I and the eating inside the university and days

parts.note: a nit, short for nitwit, is a fool
to take in food is to eat, past tense ate

explanation.surface: A fool I swallowed during my student days was never properly introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: the uninitiated have not been through a formal initiation.
explanation.definitionFit: Uninitiated describes people not admitted or inducted into a group or body of knowledge.

clue.text: Succeeded with tally of game hit

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in lists of monarchs
and means together with
a hunter's bag is the total of game shot

explanation.surface: A shooter succeeded with the day's bag of game bird hits.
explanation.definitionFit: To sandbag someone is to hit them with a sand-filled cosh.

clue.text: Colour's good in cut pepper

indicators.note: in puts the letter for good inside the shortened pepper
cut means the pepper word loses its last letter

parts.note: pimento is a sweet red pepper

explanation.surface: A colour looks good in sliced peppers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a substance that gives colour, so it stands for colour itself.

clue.text: Magnify power boost

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
to raise something is to boost it

explanation.surface: Enlarge with a power boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magnify' looks like enlarging an image, but it is the old sense of glorifying, as in 'My soul doth magnify the Lord'.
explanation.definitionFit: To magnify, in its religious sense, means to extol or glorify.

clue.text: Rice? Cut down all round on carbs for trim bod

indicators.note: cut down all round means each word loses its outer letters, leaving only the insides

explanation.surface: Reduce carbohydrates everywhere to get a trim body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bod' is slang for body. The question mark marks rice as an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arborio is a variety of short-grain Italian rice used for risotto.

clue.text: The Queen attired in impossible sport clothing

indicators.note: attired in means the queen is dressed in, so wrapped by, the other words

parts.note: out, as in out of the question, means impossible
to sport a garment is to wear it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Her Majesty dressed in impractical sportswear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like games but is the verb to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Outerwear is garments worn over other clothes, such as coats.

clue.text: Children ultimately worry cattle

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: something eating you is worrying you

explanation.surface: Children are ultimately anxious about the cows.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic word for cattle, oxen and cows.

clue.text: Girl at wedding goes on over mother being involved in proposal

indicators.note: being involved in puts the riding and mother inside the proposal

parts.note: a bid is an offer or proposal

indicators.note: over means in this down clue one word sits on top of the other

parts.note: rides is goes on, as on a horse or bus
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A girl at a wedding carries on about her mother getting involved in the proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: The proposal is not marriage but an offer, a bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid is a girl or woman who attends the bride at a wedding.

clue.text: One backed by nine points of the law … or about three points?

definitions.text: One backed by nine points of the law

indicators.note: about means around, so the word or goes round the compass letters

parts.note: W, N and E are three points of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone supported by most of the law, or by roughly three points?
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says possession is nine points of the law, so a possessor has the law largely on their side.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessor of property is backed by the saying that possession counts for most in law.

clue.text: I fall asleep with book that's sent up Italian playwright

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue means written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: to nod off is to fall asleep
a log is a book of records

explanation.surface: I doze off with a book that mocks an Italian dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' looks like mocked, but it reverses I NOD LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlo Goldoni was an eighteenth-century Venetian dramatist.

clue.text: True mind is complicated organ that is underdeveloped

indicators.note: is complicated means the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A real mind is a complicated organ, yet still immature.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a rudiment is an imperfectly developed organ or part.

clue.text: Modest girl's taking legal proceedings about male

parts.note: Una is a girl's name, here with its possessive

indicators.note: about means around, so the legal action surrounds the male

parts.note: suing is taking someone to court

explanation.surface: A modest girl is suing a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Unassuming means not pretentious or arrogant, so modest.

clue.text: Adding yeast to vegan line crackers

indicators.note: crackers is slang for mad, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Putting yeast into vegan crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' looks like biscuits, but means crazy, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Leavening means raising dough with a rising agent such as yeast.

clue.text: Large betting account, one with admissions of debt

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds at a race's start
AC or a/c is the abbreviation for account
IOUs, I owe you notes, admit a debt; one, I, is read with the OUs

explanation.surface: A big betting account belongs to someone with lots of debt notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacious means roomy, having plenty of space, so large.

clue.text: Go right through finished work

parts.note: something over is finished
a machine that runs is working

explanation.surface: Get through the job when the work is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to spread over or swarm through a place completely.

clue.text: Record time in key book

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: in puts the time letter inside the island

parts.note: a key, or cay, is a low island, an isle

explanation.surface: Recording time in a key book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like a musical key or a lock's key; it is a low island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistles are books of the New Testament, letters such as Romans.

clue.text: Recognition councillor needs to make changes

parts.note: to edit is to make changes to text

explanation.surface: A councillor needs acknowledgement to make reforms.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit means praise or acknowledgement for an achievement.

clue.text: Corporation keeping hospital billions in hitch

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the belly encloses the hospital letter

parts.note: corporation is old British slang for a large belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A company with hospitals worth billions has hit a snag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company; it is a jokey British word for a paunch. 'Hitch' is to hitchhike, thumb a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To thumb a lift is to hitch-hike, hitch for short.

clue.text: Small bundle with Internet service provider

parts.note: ISP is the abbreviation for internet service provider

explanation.surface: A little package comes with your broadband provider.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisp is a small bundle or twist of straw or hay.
